description: We are a team of first-year CSE students from College of Engineering Trivandrum (CET), interested in space, technology, problem-solving, and learning through the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are especially interested in members with skills or interest in programming, web development, UI/UX, data analysis, AI/ML, research, presentation, or creative ideas.
summary: Celestial Chronicles (also titled Celestial Relics & Sentinels) is an interactive web archive built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 that chronicles over 18 NASA satellites, landers, and rovers left on the Moon and Mars across 55 years of exploration. The platform addresses the challenge of making deep-space history engaging and accessible through an interactive 3D orbital radar, a searchable archival registry with detailed mission schematics, a side-by-side spacecraft comparison matrix, and a Deep Space Network (DSN) simulator that calculates real-time light-speed communication delays. Built using vanilla web technologies and procedural Web Audio, it preserves humanity's extraterrestrial heritage and lets users explore how both retired monuments and active transmitters continue to shape space discovery.
details:
Project Description: Celestial Relics & Sentinels

Celestial Relics & Sentinels is an interactive web-based archive that explores the history of NASA's robotic missions to the Moon and Mars. It documents satellites, landers, rovers, and other spacecraft that remain on these celestial bodies, preserving their scientific achievements and contributions to space exploration.

How does it work?

Our website provides an interactive platform where users can:

- Explore an interactive radar-style visualization of Mars.

- Discover 18+ documented NASA spacecraft and mission relics.

- Search and filter rovers, landers, orbiters, and satellites.

- Compare spacecraft through a side-by-side technical comparison matrix.

- Explore each mission's history, technical specifications, scientific instruments, and achievements.

- Use a Deep Space Network simulator to send virtual messages and understand the time radio signals take to travel across space.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes NASA's space exploration history more accessible, engaging, and easier to understand. It helps students, educators, and space enthusiasts learn about robotic missions, spacecraft technologies, planetary exploration, and communication delays. Our goal is to preserve the legacy of these missions, encourage curiosity about space science, and create awareness of humanity's achievements beyond Earth.

Technologies and Tools Used

We developed the project using:

- HTML5: Website structure and content.

- CSS3: Styling, animations, and responsive design.

- JavaScript: Interactive features, search, filtering, comparisons, and simulations.

- Web Audio API: Procedural audio and telemetry sound effects.

- NASA JPL, NASA Goddard, and Deep Space Network resources: Research and mission information.

- GitHub Pages: Website hosting and deployment.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of our project is presenting historical space missions as an interactive deep-space archive rather than a traditional information website. We combined space-themed visualizations, interactive spacecraft exploration, technical comparisons, and a simulated Deep Space Network communication experience to make learning more immersive.

Factors Considered by Our Team

While developing the project, we considered:

- Accuracy and reliability of NASA mission information.

- Ease of navigation and user experience.

- Making complex scientific information understandable.

- Interactive learning rather than presenting only static text.

- The historical and scientific importance of abandoned spacecraft.

- Accessibility across different devices and screen sizes.

- The educational value and potential impact on students and space enthusiasts.

Overall, our project aims to transform the forgotten spacecraft of the Moon and Mars into an interactive digital record of humanity's journey into space.
